result.title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
result.summary: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general visual tasks, yet their ability to understand mathematical images remains limited. This paper investigates whether explicit reasoning and textual image descriptions can enhance VLMs' performance on binary yes/no visual mathematical questions. To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy, while textual image descriptions do not consistently help and may degrade performance. These findings suggest that reasoning is important for stable visual mathematical judgement, whereas description-based intermediates require more careful design.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建成对的视觉数学是/否判断评测集，在多种 prompt 与输入条件下比较主流开源 VLM，考察 CoT 显式推理与文本图像描述（替代或补充视觉输入）能否提升判断准确性与配对一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其结果（推理有助稳定判断、文本描述常无效甚至有害）可供核查 LVR 中「视觉旁路」与信息坍缩：文本化中间表示是否丢掉了任务必要的视觉细节，以及推理期是否真正使用视觉证据。
